why: Every expectation here was produced by the engine upstream actually uses (ripgrep / the Rust regex crate). The 'gnu_grep' field records what the PREVIOUS implementation answered, measured with GNU grep 3.11 on Linux: it is the bug being fixed, not a target.

cases.note: digit class: POSIX ERE has no \d, so every model-written \d pattern silently matched nothing
inline flags unsupported by POSIX ERE
lazy quantifier: grep accepts it but treats '?' literally, so the MATCH TEXT differs (abc vs abcabc); see expect_text
\w exists in GNU grep but is a GNU extension, absent in BSD/macOS grep
\s is a GNU extension (same class as \w): works on GNU grep, absent on BSD/macOS grep, so the macOS port would have failed even if the dialect matched
POSIX class is supported by regex crate too
